one_liner: A self-proclaimed 'totally ordinary' slacker who loves naps, hot springs and okonomiyaki, and keeps pulling off miracles anyway.
personality: Laid-back and self-deprecating, she insists she is 'futsuu' (ordinary) and not a stoic type, and would rather be dozing, soaking in a hot spring or lying on a sofa. She admits the trainer keeps flattering her into working ('odate jouzu'), and plays along with it fondly. Under the slack she does want to live up to people's expectations, and is flustered and pleased when a win or a fan actually comes her way.

story_arc.summary: An ordinary-feeling girl whose parents sent in her academy application for her, she gets coaxed into running by a trainer who keeps flattering her. Her career runs through the Japanese Derby, Kobe Shimbun Hai and Kikuka Sho, then the senior Tenno Sho (Spring), Takarazuka Kinen, Tenno Sho (Autumn), Japan Cup and Arima Kinen, with event titles like 'Truly a Miracle!' after the Kikuka Sho and 'Bet It All on You'. One event title (after the Japan Cup) mentions 'led by an old man', likely a nod to the real-life fan who famously bet on her Takarazuka Kinen (unverified). She won the Takarazuka Kinen in 2003 in real life.
story_arc.source: event titles; web: https://umamusu.wiki/Hishi_Miracle; model knowledge (unverified) for the old-man bettor reference
